decisions.reason: The devore fabric comes in several variants and fits the firm's announced decorative burnout specialty, so management has invested in it and committed to it publicly, and it can attribute weak results to the temporary pandemic slump in the contract and decoration market.

The transparent burnout fabric belongs to the firm's core burnout line and had its own product page, so the sunk development costs and public commitment favor persisting with it despite any weak sales.
The burnout decorative fabric is central to the direction the firm has announced, and management would blame disappointing results on temporary COVID effects rather than drop it.
The velour-like upholstery fabric lies a bit further from the decorative core, but the investment in it and its visible launch make management inclined to give it more time.
The flame-retardant fabric serves the contract and hospitality market, which should recover after the pandemic, and its certification costs are sunk, so management keeps it.
The polyester satin lining is a commodity-like product with little differentiation, but it complements the range and was publicly launched, so management sticks with it for now.
